newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-BLACKMAR WINS HOUSTON OPEN ON FIRST EXTRA HOLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BLACKMAR WINS HOUSTON OPEN ON FIRST EXTRA HOLE.

text.p: Texas native Phil Blackmar birdied the first hole of a sudden death playoff with Kevin Sutherland on Sunday to win the 50th Houston Open and end a nine-year PGA Tour title drought.
Blackmar knocked a six-iron approach shot to three feet from the cup and tapped in his birdie putt worth $288,000 and a two-year exemption on the PGA Tour.
"Dreams do come true," said the towering 6-foot-7 (2.0 m) Texan. "In 1994, I had to go through qualifying school to regain my card and I had doubts I'd ever be here again."
Suthland and Blackmar began the day tied for the lead and each posted two-under-par 70s on Sunday.

Sutherland, who was looking for his first PGA victory, missed a potential winning putt from 20 feet on the final hole of regulation and missed another 20 footer on the first playoff hole. He got his chance at the playoff courtesy of Blackmar's double bogey on the 17th hole.
"I should have expected a roller coaster ride," Blackmar said. "After 16 I thought I had the tournament won, but after 17 I was in a state of shock."

Blackmar took a two-shot lead to the par-4 17th hole, but finished with a six when he chipped his third shot into the lake which guards the green. He had to make a downhill six-foot putt for the double bogey, falling back into a tie with Sutherland.
"When I saw him chip it into the water on 17, my mind really started racing because I knew I was back in the game," Sutherland said.

Blackmar nearly blew it again on the final hole. He hit his drive in the right rough and put his approach shot into a bunker. But he was able to get up and down for par while Sutherland two-putted for par, setting up the playoff.
"I pretty much go for broke in playoffs," said Blackmar, whose three career titles have all come from playoff wins.
"I don't know if it will always work out for me, but it has so far. I knew Kevin was already on the green, so I had to go for the pin."

Australian Steve Elkington, who lives in nearby Houston and went to college there, fired a seven-under 65 -- the low round of the day -- to finish alone in third place at 276, two shots behind Blackmar and Sutherland.
Elkington, the leading money winner on the PGA Tour this year, started the day seven shots behind the co-leaders but caught Blackmar and Sutherland at 10-under with an eagle on the par-5 15th hole.
He finished with three pars, missing a chance to make the playoff a threesome.
"I had a lot of fun out there today," said Elkington, who had his parents and dozens of college friends on hand for support.
"This is the best round I've ever had in Houston, but I just started too far back."
